findings.rationale: The contract says “Spec author | Opus … drafts specs/ADRs,” but orchestration routes planning directly to `apex-plan`, whose executor is told “Write to docs/drafts.” No step dispatches the required Opus author, so the Fable host is led to author the spec itself.

ADR-045 assigns coder dispatch to the Sonnet build orchestrator, while `parallel-codex.md` says “The host runs them as concurrent … codex exec subprocesses.” These assign the same dispatch operation to different roles.

ADR-045 says the Sonnet orchestrator dispatches Codex and Codex writes code. The live `apex-coder` instead says “only code-worker agents write files” and spawns `code-worker`, itself pinned `model: sonnet`. That creates a competing Sonnet-codes-by-default pipeline.

ADR-045 explicitly reserves the handoff and state bookkeeping for the host. The Sonnet docs agent is instructed to write the handoff, archive the spec, and rewrite `docs/status.md`, transferring those exact host duties to a worker.

findings.criterion: RULE CONTRADICTION — session and fallback routing
findings.rationale: The current contract says no `APEX_MODE` and Sonnet 5 fallback. The workflow header still requires “the fallback coder” to be Opus in an `APEX_MODE=coding` host and says the path is only for Opus fallback builds.

The session contract names Sonnet 5 as fallback. These live build/review rules repeatedly describe “Opus built (the fallback)” or route failures to “Opus fallback.” Review-family selection and failure recovery therefore disagree about which Claude model actually built the code.

`apex-code` says quota-out falls back to a fresh `model: sonnet` worker. The referenced workflow accepts only `model: opus` and declares itself Opus-fallback-only, so the documented workflow cannot execute the current fallback.

The build skill defines `coder_model: {codex|sonnet}`. Planning and the spec template define `{codex|opus}`; the template then self-contradictorily says “opus pins” the Sonnet fallback. A spec cannot choose a value accepted consistently by author and executor.

The file first says the menu is `{codex, opus}` and Opus is fallback, then says “Fallback: sonnet,” immediately followed by “apex-code's Opus builds the task” and a whole-spec `coder_model: opus` pin.
The session host is Fable 5. Research labels phase 1 as “you, in-context (Opus)” and bases its cost contract on that identity. Both cannot describe the active planning host.

The current build skill and reference set the default cap to 2. The spec template says an absent value comes from status.md and is auto-sized with fallback 3. Identical specs therefore receive different concurrency defaults.
Accepted ADR-028/029 still establish 3 on this host and fallback 3, while the live skill says default 2, citing only “A2, session-79b.” No accepted ADR amendment records the reduction.

The spec template reads `coder_models` and `max_parallel_codex` defaults from status.md, but the current status template contains only `stack` and `autonomy_level` before its live-state tables. Neither referenced field exists.

Governance says critical paths always require a live attended confirmation and “an authorising spec does not settle it,” but later says “Everything listed” in spec Permissions is pre-authorized. Critical actions listed in a spec satisfy one rule and violate the other.
Governance says spec text cannot approve critical files and AFK must park. The spec template states “Approving this spec approves all” listed actions without excluding critical paths.

Governance permanently forbids “Any modification to docs/audit/.” The permissions procedure and L4/L5 files require the agent to append every action to `docs/audit/YYYY-MM-DD.log`. An L4+ run cannot obey both.
CLAUDE.md allows merging named PRs after explicit live approval. Governance lists `git merge / merging its own PR` as permanently forbidden “regardless of who asks.”
Research instructs the agent to edit `permissions.allow` before dispatch. Governance permanently forbids actions that widen the agent's own controls and classifies permission settings as critical.

The worker contract says “Never delete anything,” while the canonical spec schema supports `Operation: delete` and authorized Delete operations. A valid deletion task is unexecutable by the named worker.
Parallel teardown says to remove the worktree “then delete the branch.” Governance permanently forbids `git branch -d / -D` at every level.
Handoff recovery mandates a WIP commit when pausing. CLAUDE.md and governance require the message to be shown and approved before every L2+ workflow commit; the handoff rule provides no gate.

Pre-flight calls Files to Change a whole-build scope lock and forbids every unlisted file. Fork handling says that when the file is elsewhere, “build in the real place” and merely flag it, which requires leaving the locked set.

The wrapper refuses a recipe-less build with exit 72 before launch, yet Verify says that if no recipe exists, write one into AGENTS.md. That recovery is unreachable and AGENTS.md is also critical host state requiring attended confirmation.

The main skill says “always dispatch through the wrapper” and raw `codex exec` is hook-blocked. Observability calls a hand-rolled raw command the default recipe except for AFK, and parallel dispatch also gives a raw command. Those documented paths are mechanically denied.
The skill says “The host runs it — never the coder subprocess judging its own output.” The dispatch pack and AGENTS contract explicitly order the coder to run and repair the verification recipe.
The main skill requires the authoritative recipe “per task, not once at the end.” Parallel integration requires it once on the integrated wave. The same parallel wave cannot use both cadences.

The post-build section says a moving tree voids a review and manual Claude gates must be pinned. It then runs `apex-reviewer` in parallel with `apex-docs-product-agent`, which writes source docs, CHANGELOG and README while that review is open.
The review is declared “advisory” and said to “never block the pipeline,” but its wrapper routing maps a BLOCK verdict to exit 67. That is a blocking pipeline result.

The agent must fill What Was Built, Specs Completed, Files Changed, Documentation Status and Current State. The current template has only Decisions, Flags, Blocked Actions and What's Next, and explicitly forbids repeating changed files/build status.

The declared inputs omit `apex-docs-product-agent` output, but Step 2 requires Documentation Status from that output and claims it was passed. A caller following the input contract cannot supply required data.

The agent still reads a bound stack `## Verification Recipe` from `stack_skills` in status.md per ADR-006, then falls back to `## Commands to run`. ADR-037 moved the sole recipe to AGENTS.md; neither current template contains those old fields/headings.
README handling requires reading the spec's `## Scope` section. The current spec template has no `## Scope`; it has Intent, Assumptions, Files, Tasks and criteria.

Files to Change is a whole-build scope lock, but the product-doc agent runs after every build and unconditionally updates CHANGELOG, with possible README edits, without requiring those files to appear in the spec. Specs omitting those paths create an off-scope post-build write.

Both AGENTS contracts tell Codex to implement `## Exact changes` and run `## Commands to run`. The canonical spec template defines neither heading; it uses Tasks and a nested Permissions/Commands table.
For the same “build specs” trigger, AGENTS requires “One spec fully at a time,” while accepted ADR-029 requires independent specs to fan into shared parallel waves.
Handoff says “Which specs finished” lives in `status.md + done/`. The session and planning contracts require every finished row to be deleted and history never stored in status.md.

Init says PROJECT.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, ROADMAP.md and status.md are “loaded by every new agent before it acts.” ADR-037 says Codex reads AGENTS.md and explicitly never reads status.md; the three project-root files are not universal context files.
Init's completion banner still says `Mode: planning`. The session contract says there is no planning mode or coding mode.
The ADR says “Codex never reads status.md,” but its decision table says status.md is read by “Both (provider-agnostic).” The intended meaning of “Both” is not reconciled.
The status template points “Model routing → ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.” CLAUDE.md explicitly says routing moved to `hooks/apex-session-context.md`, where the current table now resides.

Four live `[[memory-link]]` references remain, but a global search of the worktree's memory directories found no corresponding files. The cited entries were deleted, leaving unresolvable policy references.

Stack says the ADR-001 template and package-name warning live in `impl.md`. The new core contains neither; ADR procedure now lives in `apex-plan/references/adr-and-status-procedures.md`, and elaboration contains no package-name rule.
ADR-036 deleted bound stack/domain skills. These files still rely on “bound stack NEVER/ALWAYS,” “bound stack impl” cores, and “domain impl.md files,” describing infrastructure that no longer exists.

The reference says card source is “the project, not an APEX skill” and there is nothing to mirror, then requires regeneration when a “source APEX skill” changes and deletion when that skill is removed.
The projection table still sources a Verification Recipe from `status.md / AGENTS.md`. ADR-037 makes AGENTS.md its single home and explicitly removes status.md as a recipe source.

References point to a `Worker return contract`, `Wave domain review`, `Windows sandbox artifact ownership`, and `Cross-model review graceful-degrade`. None of those sections exists in the current apex-code SKILL.md.
Both references claim apex-plan/SKILL.md carries their trigger tables and loop rules. The skill now only points to `design-workflow.md`; the claimed content moved there.

P1's rationale treats `apex-build-wave` as “Opus-fallback-only by design.” Current routing makes Sonnet 5 the fallback. The plan does not identify updating or retiring that stale Opus workflow premise as a pending change.

ADR-045 explicitly amends fallback from Opus to Sonnet. Several older accepted ADRs still assert Opus fallback and lack a superseded/amended-by ADR-045 notice. The winner is recorded, but readers entering through the older ADRs receive stale rules.
apex-code says the technical docs agent folds the shipped capability into `overview.md`. The agent contract contains no overview read or write step, so the promised action has no executor.
Intentionally not read or judged. The standing scope lock explicitly overrides the corpus request for this file. All other requested C:/Users/User/apex cross-references were readable and audited.
